paper.paper_scope: Studies how 2.5 wt.% Si and 2.5 wt.% Al alloying affect the austenite lattice parameter (by XRD) and stacking fault energy (by TEM weak-beam dark-field dislocation separation) in three fully austenitic Fe–Ni–Cr steels derived from the Fe–Ni–Cr–Al–Si system.
paper.title: The influence of silicon and aluminum alloying on the lattice parameter and stacking fault energy of austenitic steel

unmapped_findings: TEM SFE specimens: 12.7 mm diameter cylinders machined parallel to the rolling direction, compressed to 5% true strain to introduce dislocations, then sectioned at 45° from the compression axis and electropolished in 95% acetic acid + 5% perchloric acid (b0016).

XRD: seven coupons per alloy ground to 600 grit and chemically polished 20 min in 10 water : 10 hydrogen peroxide : 1 hydrofluoric acid; Phillips X'Pert diffractometer with Cu Kα (λ = 0.154060 nm); lattice parameters from (111), (200), (220), (311) peaks extrapolated to θ = 90° (b0013).
Measured SFE values: base alloy 26.3 mJ m⁻²; 2.5 wt.% Al increases SFE by 12.0 mJ m⁻² (12–17 mJ m⁻²); 2.5 wt.% Si decreases it by 6.4 mJ m⁻² (6–7 mJ m⁻²) (b0029, b0034).

Empirical linear coefficients determined: A_LP for Si = -0.018×10⁻³ nm wt.%⁻¹ and Al = 0.582×10⁻³ nm wt.%⁻¹; A_SFE for Si = -2.6 mJ m⁻² wt.%⁻¹ and Al = 4.9 mJ m⁻² wt.%⁻¹ (Table 2, b0022, b0025, b0032).
Overestimation of austenite C content (δ_C) if Al lattice expansion is ignored ranges 0.125–0.176 wt.% (approx. 0.15 wt.%) for 1 wt.% Al in AHSS (b0026, b0027, b0034).
Elastic constants used in SFE Eq.(1): isotropic G = 74 GPa and ν = 0.3; an alternative effective G = 66 GPa, ν = 0.43 did not change the choice (b0021).
Williams and Carter correction for partial dislocation strain fields was not applied to the data; estimated to raise the 2.5 Al SFE to 44.0 ± 9.8 mJ m⁻² and others by ≤ ~1 mJ m⁻² (b0029).
